Operator: Good day, and welcome to the GlobalCom Media Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalCom Media Inc.'s Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Network Officer; Morgan Patel, Chief Commercial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I am excited to share our Q3 results, which reflect our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction. We achieved strong performance across several key areas. First, our subscriber growth and bundled offerings exceeded expectations, driving revenue momentum. Second, we continue to see strong adoption of our 5G Ultra Wideband services, leading to enhanced ARPU and fixed wireless access penetration. Third, our focus on content and media synergies has yielded impressive subscriber adds and profitability gains. Fourth, we are making significant strides in network expansion and 5G deployment. Fifth, our efforts to optimize churn through AI personalization and bundling are paying off with industry-leading retention. Sixth, we are strategically investing in fiber and edge computing, and finally, we are exploring robust shareholder returns including sustainable dividends and buybacks.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. Now, let's move on to the financial results. Our revenue for the quarter reached $28.7 billion, an increase of 4.2% compared to the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.2 billion, resulting in a margin of 39.1%, driven by our 5G fixed wireless access synergies and streaming subscriber growth. We are diligently managing our costs and optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures amounted to $8.2 billion, primarily allocated to 5G infrastructure, fiber deployment, and content acquisition.

Good afternoon, everyone—though it's morning here, thank you for joining our Q3 2024 earnings call for GlobalCom Media Inc. As we wrap up this strong quarter, let me turn to the aspect our shareholders care about most: dividend sustainability and our robust shareholder returns framework. We've built a fortress balance sheet in this capital-intensive telecom and media landscape, and I'll walk you through the metrics, trends, and strategic levers that underpin our commitment to delivering superior total shareholder returns.

First, on our dividend: GlobalCom Media has been a proud Dividend Aristocrat for 12 consecutive years, with 28 years of uninterrupted increases. Our current annualized dividend stands at $2.60 per share, reflecting a 6% hike we announced this morning—our 29th consecutive annual increase. This delivers a compelling forward yield of 4.8% based on yesterday's close, well above the S&P 500 Telecom Select Industry Index average of 3.2% and peers like Verizon at 6.5% but with our superior growth profile. For context, over the past five years, we've compounded our dividend at a 7.2% CAGR, outpacing inflation and matching the TSR of high-flyers like T-Mobile during their post-merger ramp-up.

Sustainability is rock-solid, anchored by our free cash flow generation. Q3 FCF came in at $3.4 billion, pushing TTM FCF to $13.8 billion—up 12% YoY despite the $8.2 billion in capex for 5G Ultra Wideband densification and our next-gen fiber-to-the-X deployments. This FCF comfortably covers our full-year dividend obligation of $8.9 billion, with a coverage ratio of 1.55x. Looking deeper, our payout ratio on adjusted EPS—$4.85 for FY2024 guidance—is a prudent 54%, leaving ample room for reinvestment. We've stress-tested this against industry headwinds: even in a +200bps rate hike scenario or 10% ARPU erosion from cord-cutting, our dividend remains 1.3x covered by FCF through 2026.

Let me break it down regionally, as our diversified footprint drives resilience. In North America, our wireless segment—now 65 million postpaid connections, with 5G penetration at 62%—generated $7.5 billion in TTM FCF, fueled by premium postpaid ARPU of $58.20, up 2.8% on plan mix-shift to our myPlan bundles integrating Paramount+ and Spectrum SportsNet content. This covers 45% of our dividend payout. Europe, via our Vodafone joint venture stake and standalone ops in Germany and the Nordics, added $3.2 billion FCF, benefiting from Open RAN trials reducing capex intensity by 15% and EU spectrum auctions where we secured C-band at a 20% discount to US levels. Latin America, our growth engine with 45 million subs, contributed $2.1 billion despite FX volatility, thanks to Claro's 4G/5G convergence and Claro Video streaming overtaking Netflix in Brazil market share.

Shareholder returns extend beyond the dividend. We've executed $4.2 billion in share repurchases YTD under our $10 billion authorization, retiring 2.1% of shares outstanding at an average price of $48. This opportunistic program—prioritizing when we're trading below 8x EV/EBITDA versus Comcast's 10x—has boosted EPS by 4% this year. Total capital returns for 2024 now project to $15.5 billion, or 112% of FCF, blending dividends and buybacks. Our three-year cumulative TSR stands at 28%, outperforming the S&P 500's 22% and the telecom/media peer median of 15%, driven by 15% stock appreciation plus our yields.

Strategically, we're future-proofing this profile amid 5G monetization, edge computing ramps, and the streaming wars. Capex peaks at $8.5 billion this year—down from $9.2 billion in 2023—shifting to maintenance mode at 14% of revenue by 2026, as our AI-optimized networks cut opex by 8% via predictive maintenance akin to Crown Castle's playbook. We've deleveraged net debt/EBITDA to 2.3x from 2.8x, with $4 billion in maturities refinanced at sub-4% rates. M&A firepower includes our $2.5 billion tuck-in acquisition of StreamForge, bolstering ad-tiered AVOD like Peacock's model, projecting $500 million incremental EBITDA by 2026. And we're eyeing OpenRAN scale with Nokia and Ericsson pilots, targeting 20% capex savings to fuel 5-7% annual dividend growth.

In summary, our dividend isn't just sustainable—it's a growth engine, backed by $13-15 billion annual FCF, regional diversification, and tech-led efficiencies. We reaffirm FY2024 FCF guidance of $13.5-14 billion and our mid-teens ROIC target. GlobalCom Media remains committed to maximizing shareholder value in this dynamic industry.

As we dive deeper into our financials, I'd like to spend some time on one of our highest-priority areas: network investments, particularly our 5G deployment progress and the associated capital expenditures. This remains the cornerstone of our strategy to deliver superior connectivity and media experiences, positioning us for leadership in the converged telecom-media landscape.

In Q3, we deployed a total of $4.2 billion in capital expenditures for this category, representing a 12% increase year-over-year and in line with our full-year guidance of $16 to $18 billion. Of this, approximately 52%—or $2.18 billion—was directed toward our 5G Standalone network buildout and enhancements. This includes spectrum acquisition costs, radio access network upgrades, and transport infrastructure. For context, our 5G capex has grown from $1.4 billion in Q3 2022, reflecting accelerated deployment amid favorable C-band spectrum auctions and declining equipment costs from vendors like Ericsson and Nokia.

Breaking it down further: $1.1 billion went to RAN, where we're prioritizing massive MIMO 64T64R configurations on our sub-6 GHz mid-band spectrum—primarily our 3.45-3.55 GHz holdings—to achieve median download speeds exceeding 450 Mbps. Another $650 million funded transport and core upgrades, including a shift to 400G IPoDWDM backhaul on our fiber-dense metro rings, reducing latency to under 10ms end-to-end. The remainder supported edge computing nodes and Open RAN trials.

On deployment progress, as of quarter-end, we've achieved 92% nationwide 5G coverage in our primary U.S. footprint, serving over 280 million people, up from 78% a year ago. This includes 55,000 5G sites live, with 70% now operating in true Standalone mode versus Non-Standalone overlays on our 4G LTE core. In high-density urban markets like New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago, we're at 98% coverage with mmWave at 28 GHz and 39 GHz, delivering gigabit speeds for immersive media applications—think 8K streaming and AR/VR experiences via our Stream+ platform.

Regionally, our U.S. operations lead the pack, outpacing peers like T-Mobile in SA penetration at 45% of sites versus their estimated 35%. In Europe, through our joint venture with Vodafone in the UK and Germany, we've hit 85% coverage across 120 million pops, leveraging shared 3.6 GHz spectrum and EU Digital Markets Act incentives for Open RAN. However, regulatory hurdles in Italy have slowed us to 72% there, prompting a $150 million reallocation from opex to capex for alternative sub-6 deployments. In Asia-Pacific, our Singapore and Australian footprints—covering 50 million users—are at 95% coverage, fueled by partnerships with Samsung for cloud-native RAN, where we're pioneering network slicing for low-latency gaming with Tencent and private 5G networks for media production studios.

Technically, we're not just checking boxes; we're innovating at scale. We've virtualized 40% of our RAN with Nokia's AVA platform and Ericsson's dual-mode 5G core, cutting hardware costs by 25% and enabling over-the-air software upgrades for URLLC and eMBB use cases. Our Open RAN initiative, now at 15% of new sites, includes successful interoperability tests with Qualcomm's X100 modem and DISH's stack—critical for cost discipline as we eye $500 million in savings by 2025. On the media front, edge computing investments—$200 million this quarter—position us uniquely: we've deployed 1,200 MEC nodes integrated with AWS Outposts, slashing content delivery latency for our 45 million Stream+ subscribers by 60%, boosting ARPU by 8% in Q3 through premium 5G-optimized bundles.

Strategically, these investments are yielding tangible returns. 5G service revenue grew 28% YoY to $3.1 billion, comprising 42% of our total wireless revenue, with postpaid 5G ARPU at $72—$5 above LTE peers—driven by fixed wireless access uptake, now at 2.5 million households. Churn remains industry-best at 0.92%, thanks to superior network quality scores from Opensignal, where we rank #1 in video experience. Compared to Verizon's heavier mmWave focus or AT&T's fiber pivot, our balanced sub-6/mmWave hybrid maximizes ROI, with a projected 3-year payback on 5G capex at 18-20% IRR, factoring in enterprise private networks and media ecosystem plays like our NBA AR streaming deal.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 5G capex at $2.3 billion, ramping to support 96% U.S. coverage by year-end and initial 5G RedCap deployments for IoT in 2024. Full-year capex will trend toward the high end of our guidance as spectrum refresh auctions loom, but with EBITDA margins expanding to 48%, we're funding this organically while maintaining our A- credit rating.

In summary, our 5G network isn't just an upgrade—it's a platform for media convergence, enterprise monetization, and competitive moat-building. We're on track, ahead of the curve, and delivering shareholder value.

Thank you for joining us on NexWave's Q3 earnings call—aligned with GlobalCom Media's footprint. As we wrap up a strong quarter with wireless service revenue up 3.2% year-over-year to $18.4 billion and total broadband subscribers hitting 28.7 million—driven by our FiOS Fiber expansion—let's turn to our outlook for Q4 and full-year fiscal 2025. I'll walk you through our subscriber and revenue growth guidance, grounded in the trends we're seeing across mobile, fixed broadband, and our streaming platforms like WaveStream and NexPlay.

First, on subscribers. We're guiding for net additions of 1.2 to 1.5 million total postpaid mobile subscribers in Q4, representing roughly 2.5% quarter-over-quarter growth and 4-5% year-over-year expansion. This builds on our Q3 momentum, where we added 1.1 million, fueled by our Unlimited Max 5G plan—now with over 15 million subscribers—and aggressive promotions bundling it with Apple One ecosystem services. Postpaid ARPU should tick up to $52.50-$53.00, a 2% increase, thanks to premium 5G Ultra Wideband uptake and our recent mmWave spectrum wins in the FCC's Auction 110.

On the broadband side, expect 450,000 to 550,000 FiOS Fiber net adds in Q4, pushing full-year growth to 6-7% or about 1.8 million total adds. We're on track to pass 40 million homes with gigabit-plus fiber by year-end, up from 35 million today, as capex efficiency from our Open RAN deployments in partnership with Nokia and Ericsson reduces build costs by 15-20%. This is critical in a market where cable peers like Comcast are facing 2-3% broadband losses amid cord-cutting.

For our media segment, WaveStream and NexPlay combined subscriber growth is guided at 800,000 to 1 million net adds in Q4, lifting total paid streaming subs to 22-23 million by quarter-end—a 12-15% YoY increase. This reflects our content cadence, including exclusive NFL Sunday Ticket extensions and the launch of our AI-personalized 'WaveAI Recommends' engine, which has boosted retention by 8% in beta markets. We're also seeing traction in international markets, with Latin America adds up 25% QoQ via our Vivo partnership in Brazil, where 5G fixed-wireless access is displacing satellite TV.

Regionally, North America remains our core at 85% of subs, but EMEA growth accelerates to 10% YoY on Vodafone joint ventures rolling out 5G Standalone in the UK and Germany. APAC is a wildcard—we're guiding conservatively at 5% growth amid regulatory headwinds in India, but our Starlink-like low-earth orbit trials with OneWeb could unlock 500,000 rural subs next year.

Now, revenue guidance. For Q4, we expect total consolidated revenue of $32.5 to $33.5 billion, up 5-7% year-over-year from $30.9 billion last Q4. Breaking it down: Wireless service revenue $19.0-$19.4 billion, +4-6% YoY, with equipment sales at $3.2-$3.4 billion on iPhone 16 cycle strength. Broadband and wireline: $7.8-$8.0 billion, +6-8% YoY, as fiber penetration hits 55% of our footprint. Media and advertising: $4.5-$4.7 billion, +10-12% YoY, driven by WaveStream's ad-tier launch (now 20% of subs) and CTV inventory growth amid the ongoing streaming wars—think Disney+ and Netflix price hikes creating bundling opportunities.

For full-year FY 2025, we're raising our revenue guide to $130-$133 billion, implying 4.5-6.5% growth over FY 2024's $124 billion. This assumes postpaid mobile subs reaching 85-87 million (up 5% YoY), broadband at 30 million (up 7%), and streaming at 25 million (up 18%). Adjusted EBITDA margins expand to 42-43%, with free cash flow of $18-20 billion funding $10 billion in dividends and buybacks, plus $5 billion for spectrum and fiber.

Strategically, this guidance embeds our 'Converged Edge' initiative: leveraging 5G core for low-latency media delivery, like our Xbox Cloud Gaming integration, which could add $500 million in gaming revenue by FY26. We're also monitoring macroeconomic pressures—inflation cooling helps ARPU, but potential tariff hikes on Chinese handsets could pressure equipment margins by 50-100 bps. Competitively, T-Mobile's pricing aggression and Charter's HFC upgrades are headwinds, but our 40% 5G coverage lead and exclusive NBA rights give us moat. As always, these are forward-looking statements subject to risks like regulatory changes or supply chain disruptions.

As we wrap up a transformative year in our network investments, I'd like to dive deep into our capital expenditure guidance for network investments in 2024, which remains the cornerstone of our strategy to drive broadband penetration, 5G leadership, and media delivery excellence. Our network investments are laser-focused on three pillars: enhancing wireless capacity with 5G-Advanced and future 6G readiness, accelerating fiber deployments for symmetric gigabit speeds, and bolstering our content delivery network infrastructure to support surging streaming demand amid the ongoing streaming wars.

A quick recap of 2023 performance: We deployed $18.2 billion in network capex, representing about 18% of our trailing twelve-month revenue and delivering a robust 14% return on capital employed in our core network assets. This included $9.8 billion on wireless upgrades—primarily mid-band C-band spectrum utilization in the US, where we now cover 95% of our top 100 markets—and $5.4 billion on wireline fiber, expanding our FTTH footprint to 45 million homes passed, up 22% year-over-year. The remaining $3.0 billion went to media infrastructure, including edge caching nodes optimized for AV1 codec efficiency to reduce latency for our GlobalStream+ service, which grew subscribers by 28% to 65 million.

Looking ahead to 2024, we are guiding network capex to $19.5 billion to $20.5 billion, a 7-12% increase from 2023, weighted 52% toward wireless, 32% to wireline, and 16% to media CDN and edge computing. This guidance assumes no material changes in FCC spectrum auction outcomes or supply chain disruptions from TSMC's advanced node fabs, and it excludes approximately $1.2 billion in capitalized opex for software-defined networking orchestration. On a quarterly cadence, we expect Q1 at around $4.8 billion, ramping to $5.5 billion by Q4 as seasonal 5G traffic peaks during holidays and major events like the Olympics.

Breaking it down by category: Wireless Investments: $10.1-10.6 billion (52% of total). We're doubling down on 5G Standalone core deployments, migrating from our existing NSA architecture to unlock network slicing for enterprise IoT and ultra-reliable low-latency communications. In the US, where we hold a leading 35% market share in mid-band spectrum post-2021 C-band auction—similar to Verizon's position—we'll invest $6.2 billion to densify small cells and massive MIMO antennas, targeting 99% 5G SA coverage in urban areas by year-end. This supports ARPU uplift from premium 5G plans, which already command a 15% pricing premium over 4G.

Internationally, $2.4 billion targets Europe and Latin America. In Europe, we're aligning with the EU's Gigabit Society goals, deploying Open RAN in partnership with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony across our Spanish and UK footprints—reducing vendor lock-in by 20% and capex intensity per site by 15%. In Brazil, $800 million will enhance sub-1GHz coverage to combat churn in rural areas, where we've seen 5G penetration lag at 12% versus 45% in urban São Paulo. Trends here mirror T-Mobile's US playbook: prioritizing capacity over coverage to monetize fixed wireless access, which added 2.5 million households last year.

Wireline Fiber: $6.2-6.6 billion (32% of total). Fiber remains our highest-ROI asset class, with a 25% IRR on recent XGS-PON deployments. We'll pass an additional 12 million locations, reaching 57 million homes passed, focused on greenfield builds in the US Southeast and Midwest suburbs—markets underserved by competitors like Charter's cable HFC networks. Key tech initiatives include 50G PON trials in select markets, prepping for 100G symmetrical speeds by 2026, and integrating GPON with our media bundle to drive 30% cord-cutting resistance via bundled GlobalStream+ video.

Regionally, $1.5 billion goes to APAC, where we're expanding FTTH in India through a JV with Reliance Jio, targeting 10 million new premises in Tier-2 cities amid JioFiber's aggressive pricing wars. This positions us for enterprise services growth, like private 5G campus networks for manufacturing, echoing AT&T's deal with Ford.

Media CDN and Edge: $3.2-3.3 billion (16% of total). With global video traffic projected to hit 80% of IP traffic per Cisco's VNI forecast—fueled by AI-generated content and 8K streaming—we're investing in a distributed edge cloud. This includes 2,500 new Points of Presence with NVIDIA GPU acceleration for real-time transcoding, cutting tail latency by 40% for live sports on our platform. In the US, $1.2 billion enhances peering with hyperscalers like AWS and Google Cloud, optimizing for our 4K/8K HDR feeds. Europe gets $700 million for compliance with GDPR data localization and DMA regulations, while $500 million in emerging markets supports mobile-first video, countering TikTok and YouTube's dominance.

Strategically, this capex envelope reflects three insights shaping our Telecom-Media convergence playbook. First, spectrum efficiency amid scarcity: With no major US auctions until 2026, we're emphasizing dynamic spectrum sharing and mmWave beamforming to squeeze 30% more throughput from existing holdings, much like Dish Network's bold 5G bet. Second, AI and edge monetization: Investments in disaggregated RAN and MEC will enable new revenue streams—think AR/VR metaverse slicing and AI inference at the edge—projected to add $2 billion in service revenue by 2026. Third, sustainability and efficiency: 25% of capex qualifies for US IRA tax credits via low-power base stations and recycled fiber optics, targeting a 20% reduction in energy per bit versus 2023 baselines, aligning with GSMA's net-zero goals.

Risks to this guidance include supply chain volatility in RF chips from Qualcomm and fiber preforms from Corning, or slower-than-expected FWA adoption if economic headwinds persist. Upside levers: Accelerated enterprise 5G wins or M&A in fiber-rich assets like Cogent or Frontier, which we're monitoring closely.

In summary, this $19.5-20.5 billion network capex guidance fuels 3-5% service revenue growth and 200-300bps EBITDA margin expansion in 2024, positioning GlobalCom Media as the converged leader in a 5G-media world.

I'll now turn to our churn rate analysis, where we continue to demonstrate industry-leading retention dynamics across our integrated telecom and media portfolio. For Q3 FY2024—aligned with our calendar—our blended postpaid churn rate across mobile, broadband, and video services came in at 1.12% monthly, a 15 basis point improvement year-over-year from 1.27% and flat sequentially. This marks our 11th straight quarter of sequential churn stabilization or improvement, underscoring the stickiness of our bundled offerings in a hyper-competitive landscape dominated by 5G proliferation, cord-cutting pressures, and the rise of pure-play OTT disruptors like Netflix and Disney+.

Segment trends: Postpaid Mobile (52% of revenue mix): Churn ticked down to 0.85% monthly, our lowest in three years, beating consensus estimates of 0.92%. This reflects a 22 bps YoY decline, driven by our aggressive 5G Ultra Wideband rollout—now covering 85% of our top 100 U.S. markets—and superior mid-band spectrum holdings (C-band and 3.45 GHz). Family plan penetration hit 68%, up from 62% YoY, as customers lock in multi-line discounts amid rising standalone plan prices from rivals like T-Mobile and Verizon. However, we saw pockets of pressure from price-sensitive millennials switching to MVNOs like Mint Mobile, which accounted for ~15% of gross losses.

Fixed Broadband (28% of mix): At 0.98% monthly, we're outperforming Comcast's reported 1.15% and Charter's 1.08%, thanks to our DOCSIS 4.0 upgrades delivering symmetrical gigabit speeds to 45 million homes passed. YoY churn improved 18 bps, but sequential uptick was due to seasonal back-to-school moves and competition from fiber overbuilders like AT&T Fiber and Verizon Fios in the Northeast. ARPU uplift from 2 Gbps tiers helped offset this, with low churn cohorts (under 0.8%) now representing 60% of our base.

Video and Streaming (20% of mix, including linear pay-TV and our direct-to-consumer StreamGlobal): This remains our highest-churn segment at 2.45% monthly, down modestly from 2.62% YoY but up 5 bps sequentially amid intensified cord-cutting. Linear MVPD churn was 3.1%, pressured by NBA and NFL rights fragmentation, while our skinny bundle and ad-supported streaming tier held at 1.8%. Netflix's password crackdown indirectly benefited us, adding 150k net adds, but Disney Bundle cross-promos with Hulu drove 8% of losses.

Key drivers from our regression analysis of ~2.5 million voluntary disconnects: Positive drivers (60% of retention lift): Bundling economics—75% of our lowest-churn customers (under 0.7%) are on quad-play packages, delivering 25% ARPU premiums and 40% lower churn vs. single-play. Network superiority: 5G SA core deployment reduced latency-related complaints by 35%, correlating to a 12 bps churn reduction. Personalization tech: Our AI-powered Customer 360 platform enabled hyper-targeted retention offers—e.g., "win-back" campaigns with 65% uptake, saving $120M in annualized revenue.

Negative drivers (40% of gross losses): Macro pressures—inflation-adjusted price increases (avg. 7%) drove 28% of churn. Competitive intensity—OTT migration explained 22% of video losses. Operational headwinds—legacy copper decommissioning in Europe added 15 bps.

Regional commentary: North America (85% of subs): U.S. postpaid mobile churn at 0.82% leads the industry. Europe (10% of subs): Blended churn at 1.48%, higher due to GDPR-mandated porting ease. Asia-Pacific/LatAm (5% of subs): Elevated at 1.75% from prepaid dominance, but our Starlink backhaul pilots stabilized rural Mexico churn at 2.2%.

Strategic insights: We're not complacent—our Net Promoter Score climbed to 62, aiming for 70. Initiatives include GenAI chatbots for 90% issue resolution under 2 minutes, exclusive Premier League digital rights, and predictive analytics flagging at-risk subs 45 days early. We guide blended churn to 1.05-1.10% for FY2024, with postpaid mobile sub-0.8%, positioning us for 2.5-3% service revenue growth.

I'll now turn to our Content and Media segment, which continues to be a cornerstone of our diversified portfolio, powering both standalone growth and synergies with our broadband and wireless businesses. This segment encompasses our flagship StreamHub SVOD platform, ad-supported tiers including our FAST channels like RetroTV and SportsClips, linear TV bundles via Xfinity Media partnerships, content licensing to third parties, and sports rights including our NHL regional sports networks and upcoming NBA deals.

Revenue: Content and Media generated $2.45 billion in Q3—adjusted for our quarter—up 12% year-over-year and 5% sequentially. This marks our eighth straight quarter of double-digit YoY growth, outpacing the broader industry amid ongoing cord-cutting pressures. Subscription revenue—the lion's share at $1.72 billion, or 70% of segment total—grew 15% YoY, fueled by net subscriber adds and ARPU expansion. Our StreamHub direct-to-consumer service was the standout, hitting $1.1 billion, up 18%, thanks to hits like our original series Empire of Shadows and the live sports bundle.

Advertising revenue reached $520 million, up 8% YoY, with AVOD and FAST channels contributing $320 million. Impressions grew 22% to 45 billion, driven by our integration of connected TV inventory with Paramount Global's ad tech stack post our deepened partnership. Political ad spend ahead of upcoming elections added a nice tailwind. Content licensing and other rounded out at $210 million, flat YoY but with upside from syndicating Empire clips to international AVOD platforms.

Subscriber metrics: We ended Q3 with 45.2 million paid digital subscribers across StreamHub and premium linear bundles, up 2.1 million net adds quarter-over-quarter and 4.8 million YoY. Churn held steady at 1.2% monthly, below our 1.5% target, thanks to our AI-driven retention engine which uses machine learning to personalize recommendations and flag at-risk users 72 hours early—reducing voluntary churn by 15%. Paid StreamHub subs hit 32.5 million, with 1.8 million net adds, including 850,000 from broadband bundling promotions. ARPU climbed to $8.45, up 4% YoY and 1% QoQ, driven by tiered pricing (our new $9.99 ad-light tier converted 25% of trials) and upsell to sports add-ons amid the NHL playoffs. Free tier users grew to 18 million MAUs, priming the funnel with a 12% conversion rate to paid.

Profitability remains robust. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $785 million, up 14% YoY, delivering a 32% margin—expansion of 120 basis points from last year. This was achieved despite $45 million in higher original content amortization for Empire Season 2 and live sports. Cost discipline was key: we realized $120 million in savings through cloud migration to AWS Media Services, cutting encoding costs 28%, and rights renegotiations with ESPN for linear carriage. Excluding one-time sports overages, core margins hit 35%.

Regionally, North America drove 85% of revenue at $2.08 billion, up 13% YoY, with U.S. broadband bundling accounting for 40% of adds. EMEA grew 25% to $250 million, led by StreamHub launches in the UK and Germany, where we hit 2.5 million subs via bundling with Vodafone carriage deals. LatAm was the fastest grower at 35% to $120 million, though profitability lagged at 22% margins due to forex headwinds from the weakening Brazilian real; we're countering with local content like our telenovela co-productions with Globo.

Strategically, we're leaning into hyper-personalization via AI and 5G: Our StreamHub 2.0 platform now leverages edge computing on our 5G network for sub-2-second latency on live events, boosting engagement 18%—think NHL games streamed at 4K to mobile users without buffering. Ecosystem partnerships: Beyond Paramount, we're in talks for a Disney+ bundle, targeting 10% ARPU lift. Our FAST portfolio now rivals Roku Channel's scale, with 150 channels pulling 5 billion hours viewed YTD. Content flywheel: Capex here was $650 million, focused on 12 new originals and sports rights totaling $2.5 billion over three years—competitive with Warner Bros. Discovery's slate but with better ROI at 2.5x vs. industry 1.8x. We're also monetizing UGC via creator funds, adding $50 million in ancillary revenue.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 segment revenue growth of 10-12% YoY, with EBITDA margins at 31-33%, assuming stable ad markets and no major macro shocks. Subscriber adds should moderate to 1.5-1.8 million as we lap tough comps, but ARPU trajectory remains upward. This segment isn't just growing—it's compounding value through tech-enabled stickiness and cross-sell with our core telecom assets.

Taylor Kim: Thank you, Jordan. I would like to provide an update on our network performance and expansion. We continue to enhance our 5G network, achieving wider coverage and faster speeds, with 92% nationwide reach and median downloads over 450 Mbps through massive MIMO upgrades. Our network reliability remains high at industry-leading levels, and we are investing in advanced technologies like Open RAN and edge computing to further improve performance—virtualizing 40% of RAN and deploying 1,200 MEC nodes for low-latency media. We are also focused on optimizing our network for emerging applications like IoT, network slicing for gaming, and private 5G for enterprises, all while targeting 20% energy efficiency gains aligned with GSMA net-zero goals.

Morgan Patel: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We saw strong growth in subscriber additions—1.1 million postpaid mobile in Q3, plus broadband and streaming gains—driven by our innovative product offerings like Unlimited Max 5G bundles and AI-personalized content, alongside targeted marketing campaigns. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, with Net Promoter Score at 62 and churn at blended 1.12% monthly, and we are continuously working to improve the customer experience across all touchpoints through GenAI chatbots and predictive retention. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships—like Vodafone JVs and Paramount integrations—to offer bundled services and enhance customer value, with quad-play penetration driving 40% lower churn.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your subscriber acquisition costs and your strategy for reducing churn, specifically with regards to postpaid mobile trends and bundling impacts?

Morgan Patel: Good morning, Mike. On subscriber acquisition costs, we're seeing stabilization at around $450 per postpaid add, down 5% YoY due to efficient digital campaigns and family plan uptake at 68%. For churn reduction—our postpaid mobile at 0.85% monthly—we're leveraging bundling, where quad-play customers show 40% lower rates, and AI tools like Customer 360 for 65% win-back success. This has saved $120 million annualized, and we expect further improvement with GenAI chatbots targeting sub-0.8% in FY2025.

This supports Open RAN at 15% of sites for $500 million savings by 2025. On capex, it enables our $19.5-20.5 billion 2024 guide, shifting to 14% of revenue maintenance by 2026 while funding 99% urban 5G SA coverage—no change to the range.
